item.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
item.description:
Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
November 22, 202612:34 PM ET
By
Kate Bartlett
Fiona Mogane, 13, contributed the story "Lindani's Modelling Journey" to From Gomora to the World. Stories from Alex, a new book of short stories written by kids who are part of the "Read Alex" literacy program in Johannesburg. Participants in weekly classes wrote stories drawing on their own lives.
Madalene Cronje for NPR
hide caption
toggle caption i
Madalene Cronje for NPR
JOHANNESBURG — It's an ordinary Saturday morning in Alexandra township, known simply as Alex or sometimes dubbed Gomora, a reference to the biblical city of Gomorrah that was known for its wickedness.
That nickname stems from Alexandra's high crime rates. It's a high-density area, where modest brick houses and tin shacks stretch as far as the eye can see and rotting garbage piles up along potholed streets.
But that image doesn't intrude on an event at a small building at the Kwabhekilanga Sports Ground. There's a palpable sense of excitement. Something different is happening this weekend and community members have turned up for it.

COP31 President Murat Kurum, center, leaves a closing plenary session at the U.N. Climate Summit, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey. Nearly 200 countries failed to reach an agreement on whether they should move away from fossil fuels like coal and natural gas.
Khalil Hamra/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Khalil Hamra/AP
ANTALYA, Turkey – International climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, broke down in overtime hours with a disagreement over how to address fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.
On Sunday, delegates from nearly 200 countries failed to reach an overall agreement covering targets for electrification, finance to help developing countries adapt to the impacts of climate change, and how to respond to the fact that the planet will soon breach a key warming threshold.

item.title: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
item.description:
Politics
Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
November 21, 20265:40 PM ET
By
The Associated Press
President Trump speaks at a news conference in the James Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, in Washington.
Jacquelyn Martin/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Jacquelyn Martin/AP
NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to a new executive order.
The companies must also coordinate with the White House and U.S. agencies on "appropriate responses" to any such requests, the order issued late Friday says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.
The order is the Republican administration's latest effort to resist what are expected to be wide-ranging and aggressive oversight efforts from Democrats when they take over Congress in January.
